setup_summary.text: Next report is fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-01-19 after the close, about 80 days from today. Consensus is EPS $1.42 and revenue $8.16B. Whisper, options-implied move and beat/miss record are not available. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is about 1.9%.

Q3 2026 (call date not given in the sources) was another record quarter: revenue of about $8B (+8.7% y/y; +6.4% adjusted for BTIG and securities losses) and diluted EPS of $1.34 (+10% y/y). That includes about $0.07 of reserve build, so EPS growth was about 16% excluding the build. Q3 EPS was slightly below Q2's $1.35.
Management raised full-year guidance on the Q3 call: net revenue growth of 8-9% (6-7% ex-BTIG), up from 5-7%. Operating leverage is now about 300bp (about 400bp ex-BTIG), up from 200bp and 300bp.

Q4 guidance, year over year: taxable-equivalent NII +6-7%; fee revenue +13-14%, with roughly half of that from BTIG; noninterest expense about +8% (about +4% ex-BTIG). Net interest margin (NIM) is expected to rise by a similar amount to Q3's 5bp, from 2.84%.

My arithmetic from the guidance: 8-9% growth on FY2025 revenue of $28.66B, with H1 2026 at $15.00B and Q3 at roughly $7.97B (7.33B x 1.087), implies Q4 revenue of about $7.98-8.27B. Consensus of $8.16B sits in the upper half of that range. This is derived arithmetic, not company-stated, and the guidance basis is assumed to match reported net revenue.

Comparator problem in the derived consensus rows: F.49 and F.51 show Q4 consensus growth of +11.3% (revenue) and +16.5% (EPS), but they compare Q4 2026 with Q3 2025 ($7.33B and $1.22). Against Q4 2025, backed out as FY2025 less H1 2025 less Q3 2025, revenue is about $7.36B and EPS is $1.26. Consensus then implies about +10.8% revenue growth and about +12.7% EPS growth.

Capital: CET1 was 10.8% at quarter end (flat q/q), but the AOCI-adjusted ratio fell 30bp to 9.1%. RWA growth of $12B and rate/spread moves of about 40bp more than offset about 30bp of retained earnings. Buybacks were paused in Q3 and management expects to resume them 'over the next quarter or two'.

On 2026-10-30 USB closed a sale of 1,000,000 depositary shares, each 1/25th of a $25,000-liquidation Series P fixed-rate-reset preferred share. That is about $1.0B of new preferred. The coupon and use of proceeds are not in the filing.
The most recent filed quarter (Q2 2026) had revenue of $7.71B (+10.1%), EPS of $1.35 (+21.6%) and net income of $2.18B (+19.9%). BTIG closed 2026-06-01, so Q3 was the first full quarter of BTIG.

Q4 fee growth of 13-14% is below Q3's 14.9%, and management flagged mortgage drag from higher rates and the normalisation of unusual gains in 'other' revenue. NII momentum is the offset. The risk is modestly skewed to an in-line or slight miss unless NII and capital markets come in at the high end.

consensus.text: Consensus is $1.42, which is +12.7% against the backed-out Q4 2025 EPS of $1.26 (FY $4.62 less H1 $2.14 less Q3 $1.22). The sheet's +16.5% uses Q3 2025 as the base.

view.text: $1.42 roughly equals Q3 ex-reserve-build, so it assumes little reserve build and offsetting moves between higher NII and seasonally lower fees. Expense growth stepping up (ex-BTIG about 4% in Q4 versus 2.0% in Q3), plus any further build from card and Amazon book growth, is the main downside. The new Series P preferred adds dividend cost to common EPS; the coupon is unknown.

Drivers are about $10B per quarter of fixed-rate repricing at about 125bp better, floating-rate mix at 30% of earning assets and the full-quarter Amazon card book. Offsets are deposit costs (+7bp q/q in Q3, about 50% beta assumed) and further rate hikes.

since_filing.text: The 10-Q (filed 2026-08-06) covered Q2: EPS $1.35, NIM 2.79%, CET1 10.8%. Since then, Q3 reported EPS of $1.34, NIM of 2.84%, a stable CET1 of 10.8% and an AOCI-adjusted CET1 of 9.1%. Q3 results come from the call transcript; the Q3 10-Q and press release are not in the sources, and the call date is not given.

Guidance was raised on the Q3 call, with full-year revenue growth to 8-9% and operating leverage to about 300bp. This is the newest company view and supersedes the prior 5-7% and 200bp that the call itself cites. The prior guidance document is not in the sources.
The buyback was paused in Q3, after $203M of repurchases in Q2 under the $5.0B program (about $3.9B remaining at Q2). The newer call is the source for the pause and the restart timing.

Rates moved sharply in Q3 and the call refers to a September Fed rate hike. The 10-Q's net interest income sensitivity was roughly neutral for a 50bp move, and the call moves toward asset sensitivity. Treasury rate and spread moves cut the AOCI-adjusted CET1 ratio by about 40bp.

The Amazon small business co-brand card portfolio was onboarded. It added about $900M to Q3 average loans and $1.7B to period-end loans, and Q4 gets a full quarter. A first USDBC stablecoin pilot launched in September, with management saying client demand is limited and the product needs regulatory approval.

BTIG, which closed 2026-06-01, contributed $226M of fee revenue in Q3. Management targets capital markets rising from 8% to 10% or more of revenue over three to five years and will share more at a conference later this fall.

On 2026-10-30 USB closed the issuance of about $1.0B of Series P fixed-rate-reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred (via depositary shares). The 10-Q shows $6.8B of preferred outstanding at the end of Q2, and Series M, J and N become redeemable from April 2026 and January/April 2027. Whether any is being refinanced is not disclosed.

key_debates.question: Can NIM keep expanding toward 3% in 2027 as rates rise and deposit competition builds?

bull.text: Fixed-rate asset repricing of about $10B per quarter at about 125bp better, a shift to floating-rate C&I, CRE and card loans, a stronger deposit mix and the Amazon book support another +5bp in Q4. Management says mix and repricing outweigh deposit-beta competition.

bear.text: Deposit costs rose 7bp in Q3 and a roughly 50% beta is assumed. The firm has historically been liability-sensitive to short rates, and a flatter curve or tougher deposit competition could stall the margin. The Q2 10-Q showed essentially flat NII for a +50bp shock.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 NIM versus about 2.89-2.90%, deposit cost and beta trends, and whether the 3% target is repeated at the January 2027 call.

key_debates.question: Is revenue growth from fees and BTIG durable, or flattered by unusual items?

bull.text: Fees grew 14.9% in Q3 across most categories. Corporate payments grew about 19%, legacy capital markets about 10% and BTIG about $200M per quarter, and guidance for Q4 is still +13-14%.

bear.text: Q3 'other' revenue included gains that should normalise to $120-150M. Higher rates weigh on mortgage, merchant is about flat, and BTIG is market-sensitive and a high-expense business, which management itself says would push the efficiency ratio up if it grows faster.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 fee growth against 13-14%, the BTIG contribution against about $200M, and the size of the 'other' revenue line.

key_debates.question: Will capital allow buybacks to resume, and how fast?

bull.text: The company generated 33bp of capital after dividends in Q3. Management has high confidence in capital build, targets a 70-75% payout, and the March 2026 capital proposals are expected to be favorable.

bear.text: RWA growth ($12B in Q3, partly the Amazon portfolio), higher Treasury yields and heavy loan demand cut the AOCI-adjusted CET1 by 30bp, and BTIG's trading book enters the market-risk rule in Q3. Management ties the restart to rates, loan demand and regulation.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 CET1 and AOCI-adjusted CET1, any repurchase disclosed in the 10-K, and the final form of the capital and tailoring rules.

key_debates.question: Does credit stay benign as rates rise and card and C&I growth continue?

bull.text: Q3 NCOs fell to 51bp and NPAs fell 1.6% q/q. Card FICO bands have marginally improved and delinquencies have trended lower, and the consumer is not showing stress.

bear.text: Q3 included an unspecified reserve build costing about $0.07 of EPS, and management flags CRE as the watch area as rates rise. Card and Amazon-related growth continues to add reserve needs. The 10-K flagged office CRE and NDFI lending as pressure points.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 provision versus net charge-offs, the allowance ratio, and CRE and NDFI delinquency trends.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Revenue of about $8.25B or more, above consensus and at the top of what guidance implies. EPS is above $1.45 from NIM near 2.90%, strong capital markets and corporate payments, benign credit with no meaningful reserve build, and a buyback restart announced. This case combines the favourable ends of the Q3 trends, which is my scenario, not a company statement.

triggers: Capital markets and BTIG above about $200M
No reserve build and NCOs at or below 51bp
Buybacks resume in Q4 or are signalled for Q1

description.text: Revenue of about $8.0-8.2B and EPS around $1.40-1.42, in line with consensus and within the guided ranges. NII growth of 6-7%, fee growth of 13-14%, expense growth of about 8% and a NIM of about 2.89%. A small further reserve build is offset by lower 'other' fees. The buyback restart is flagged for Q1. The historical average post-earnings move is about 1.9%.

Revenue of about $7.95B or less and EPS at or below about $1.35. Fees soften on mortgage and capital markets, 'other' revenue normalises and expenses grow faster than guided. A larger reserve build from card, Amazon or CRE adds pressure, and NIM stalls on deposit competition. The buyback restart is delayed on RWA or rates, and the AOCI-adjusted CET1 stays weak.

claim.text: Deposit costs and rates: deposit costs rose 7bp in Q3 with about 50% beta assumed, and further Fed hikes could compress the margin if funding competition intensifies. The 10-Q's sensitivity was neutral to +/-50bp.

Capital: higher Treasury rates and spreads and RWA growth reduced the AOCI-adjusted CET1 by 30bp, and the pause in buybacks shows the constraint. Net unrealized AFS losses were $4.4B at Q2, and a fixed-rate securities book remains exposed to the rate backup.

Credit: the reserve build cost $0.07 in Q3, the card book is growing quickly including the new Amazon portfolio, and management is watching CRE as rates rise. The 10-K also flagged office CRE and NDFI exposure.

Capital markets and BTIG: fee growth now leans on market-sensitive revenue, with BTIG at about $200-226M per quarter and capital markets being a higher-efficiency-ratio business. The 10-K flagged integration and cross-border risks, and BTIG enters market-risk capital from Q3.

Interchange and regulation: a revised Visa/Mastercard injunctive settlement with lower interchange fees was preliminarily approved in June 2026, with a final approval hearing on 2026-11-16. The 10-K also lists credit card interest-rate caps as a risk factor, and Category II transition rules are pending.

Deposit disintermediation: stablecoin and AI cash-sorting threats are being discussed. Management says it has not seen AI agents interact with the bank, and the stablecoin pilot has limited client demand, but the 10-K flagged deposit loss to stablecoins under the GENIUS Act.

questions_for_management.question: Did Q4 include any reserve build tied to the Amazon portfolio or card growth, and what is the allowance coverage on the Amazon book?

why.text: Q3 EPS carried about $0.07 of reserve build and the Amazon book adds $1.7B of period-end loans. Consensus $1.42 is about equal to Q3 ex-build.

questions_for_management.question: What is the coupon and intended use of the $1.0B Series P preferred? Does it refinance Series J, M or N, and what is the net effect on preferred dividends in 2027?

why.text: The 8-K does not disclose pricing or use of proceeds. Several existing series become callable from 2026-2027 and preferred dividends reduce common EPS.

questions_for_management.question: What are the conditions and the likely size of the buyback restart, and how much capital headroom is assumed on AOCI-adjusted CET1, Category II and RWA growth?

why.text: The restart is guided only to 'a quarter or two' and depends on rates, loan demand and regulation. The AOCI-adjusted ratio fell to 9.1%.

questions_for_management.question: Why does ex-BTIG expense growth step up from 2.0% in Q3 to about 4% in Q4, and what is included (incentives, marketing, technology)?

why.text: Guidance implies the ex-BTIG expense run-rate doubles while full-year operating leverage was just raised to 300bp.

questions_for_management.question: What is the 2027 NIM trajectory under different Fed paths, and how much of the 3% target relies on deposit beta at or below 50% and on the curve?

why.text: Management reiterates a path to 3% in 2027 while assuming about 50% beta and a couple of further hikes, and has historically been liability-sensitive to short rates.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 run-rate for BTIG and capital markets by business, and how much of the $226M in Q3 was seasonal or market-driven?

why.text: The CFO expects about $200M, below Q3's $226M, and capital markets is intended to reach 10% or more of revenue.

questions_for_management.question: Which other-revenue items were unusual in Q3, and what is the 2027 outlook for mortgage and merchant fees at current rates?

why.text: Other revenue is expected to normalise to $120-150M, mortgage growth is limited by rates and merchant is about flat.

questions_for_management.question: What is the exposure of the commercial real estate and NDFI books to higher long rates, and why did NDFI balances run off in Q3?

why.text: C&I balances were flat q/q on NDFI runoff and unmet return hurdles, and management names CRE as the rate-sensitive watch area.
